llm-01.back: For $q,k$ with i.i.d. zero-mean, unit-variance components, $q\cdot k$ has variance $d_k$. Scaling by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ keeps logits at unit variance, preventing softmax saturation and vanishing gradients for large $d_k$.

llm-01.front: Multi-head attention: formula, and why multiple heads?
llm-01.back:
$$\mathrm{head}_i=\mathrm{Attention}(QW_i^Q,\,KW_i^K,\,VW_i^V)$$
$$\mathrm{MHA}(Q,K,V)=\mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1,\dots,\mathrm{head}_h)\,W^O$$
Heads let the model jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions; a single head would average them away.

llm-01.front: Write the sinusoidal positional encodings used in the original Transformer.
llm-01.back:
$$PE_{(pos,2i)}=\sin\!\left(\frac{pos}{10000^{2i/d_{model}}}\right),\qquad PE_{(pos,2i+1)}=\cos\!\left(\frac{pos}{10000^{2i/d_{model}}}\right)$$
For any fixed offset $k$, $PE_{pos+k}$ is a linear function of $PE_{pos}$, making relative positions easy to express.

llm-06.front: Kaplan et al.: how does loss scale with model size $N$ (data unconstrained)?
llm-06.back: A power law: $L(N)\approx\left(N_c/N\right)^{\alpha_N}$ with $\alpha_N\approx 0.076$. Analogous laws hold for dataset size ($\alpha_D\approx 0.095$) and compute ($\alpha_C$), spanning several orders of magnitude.

llm-06.front: What is the practical use of scaling laws when planning a training run?
llm-06.back: They let you predict final loss from $(N, D, C)$ before training, choose compute-optimal allocation between model size and tokens, and detect when a run is data- or capacity-bottlenecked (curves bend away from the power law).

llm-07.front: Chinchilla's compute-optimal rule of thumb: how many training tokens per parameter?
llm-07.back: Roughly $D\approx 20N$ tokens per parameter — model size and data should be scaled **equally**: $N\propto C^{0.5}$, $D\propto C^{0.5}$. Chinchilla (70B, 1.4T tokens) beat Gopher (280B) at the same compute.

llm-15.front: How does RoPE encode position, and what property does it give attention scores?
llm-15.back: Each 2-D pair of query/key features is rotated by angle $m\theta_i$ at position $m$ ($\theta_i=10000^{-2i/d}$). Then $\langle f_q(x,m), f_k(y,n)\rangle$ depends only on the **relative** offset $m-n$, giving relative-position awareness with absolute-position implementation.

llm-15.front: Why does RoPE decay attention with distance?
llm-15.back: The multi-frequency rotations progressively de-phase query/key pairs as $|m-n|$ grows, so inner products (hence logits) shrink on average with distance — a useful inductive bias for language.

llm-24.front: Write the DPO loss for preference pair $(y_w \succ y_l)$ given prompt $x$.
In what sense is the language model 'secretly a reward model' in DPO?
llm-24.back: The KL-constrained RLHF optimum is $\pi^*(y|x)\propto\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x)e^{r(x,y)/\beta}$, so $r(x,y)=\beta\log\frac{\pi^*(y|x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x)}$ (up to a prompt-only term). Substituting this into the Bradley–Terry likelihood removes the explicit reward model and RL loop.

llm-28.front: What is the core idea of FlashAttention?
llm-28.back: Compute **exact** attention with tiling and an online softmax so the $N\times N$ score matrix is never materialized in HBM. Work happens in SRAM tiles; HBM traffic drops from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N^2 d^2 / M)$ accesses ($M$ = SRAM size), and backward recomputes tiles instead of storing them.

llm-28.front: State the online softmax update when merging a new tile (running max $m$, normalizer $\ell$).
llm-28.back:
$$m^{\mathrm{new}}=\max(m,\tilde m),\qquad \ell^{\mathrm{new}}=e^{m-m^{\mathrm{new}}}\,\ell+e^{\tilde m-m^{\mathrm{new}}}\,\tilde\ell$$
The output accumulator is rescaled by $e^{m-m^{\mathrm{new}}}$ before adding the new tile's contribution — numerically stable and single-pass.

llm-28.front: Why is attention memory-bound rather than compute-bound on GPUs?
llm-28.back: Standard attention does $O(N^2)$ reads/writes of scores/probabilities to HBM while doing relatively little math per byte (low arithmetic intensity). GPU FLOPs vastly outstrip HBM bandwidth, so runtime is dominated by data movement — the quantity FlashAttention minimizes.

cv-07.front: How does ViT turn an image into transformer tokens?
cv-07.back: Split the image into $P\times P$ patches ($N=HW/P^2$ of them), flatten each and linearly project to $d$ dims, prepend a learnable [CLS] token, add learned position embeddings — then run a standard Transformer encoder.

cv-07.front: Why does ViT need more data than CNNs to train from scratch?
cv-07.back: It lacks convolutional inductive biases (locality, translation equivariance, 2-D structure), so those regularities must be learned from data. With large-scale pretraining (ImageNet-21k/JFT) ViT matches or beats CNNs, and scales better.

reg-19.back: Bin predictions by confidence; then $$\mathrm{ECE}=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\frac{|B_m|}{n}\,\bigl|\mathrm{acc}(B_m)-\mathrm{conf}(B_m)\bigr|$$ — the confidence-weighted gap between accuracy and confidence.

reg-19.front: What is temperature scaling and why is it attractive in regulated settings?
reg-19.back: Divide logits by a single scalar $T>1$ fitted on validation NLL: $\hat p=\mathrm{softmax}(z/T)$. It changes confidence but **not** the argmax (accuracy preserved), has one parameter (hard to overfit), and is trivial to audit.

reg-20.front: State the split conformal prediction coverage guarantee.
reg-20.back: With exchangeable calibration data, form prediction sets from the $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n$ empirical quantile $\hat q$ of nonconformity scores: $C(x)=\{y: s(x,y)\le\hat q\}$. Then $$P\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{test}}\in C(X_{\mathrm{test}})\bigr)\ge 1-\alpha$$ — distribution-free, finite-sample, **marginal** coverage.

reg-20.front: What conformal prediction does NOT guarantee (common misreadings).
reg-20.back: No conditional coverage (per-input or per-group) without extra assumptions; no validity under distribution shift that breaks exchangeability; and set size (efficiency) depends entirely on the underlying score/model quality.
